disclaimer: This directory was compiled with AI (Claude) assistance from publicly available sources. Every one of the 132 listed rows has now been through a deep re-verification pass and carries the sources used to check it. It remains INCOMPLETE: it covers 132 of roughly 198 ABA-accredited US law schools, and the gap is systematic — the original pass worked alphabetically by state and stopped after New York. Two things to read carefully before drawing conclusions from a tier chip. First, a 'none' or 'standalone' tier means the parent university runs no research-computing resource; it does not mean no compute, because NSF ACCESS allocates national supercomputing time to any researcher at a US academic institution in any field at no cost. Second, a high tier does not guarantee law-school access: some centers list the schools they serve, and Law is not always among them. Run audit.py before submitting a correction.
